sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: This rare cactus is native to Nuevo León and Tamaulipas, Mexico. Its small basal body is often partly hidden in the ground, while narrow grey-green tubercles may extend to about 19 cm long and only a few millimetres wide. The yellow flower has an orange centre.

sections.title: Image and uses
sections.text: The plate shows the elongated tubercles and yellow-orange flower, but does not clearly show the buried basal body. No edible use was verified. Kew reports the species as Critically Endangered; avoid implying that the illustration depicts an ordinary, fully exposed plant.

sections.title: Related cactus
sections.text: Astrophytum ornatum is another Mexican species in the genus, but has a broad, ribbed, star-like stem rather than the long tentacle-like tubercles of A. caput-medusae.
